questions.question: In 1651, John Milton published 'Defensio pro Populo Anglicano' as a direct Latin rebuttal to which defense of Charles I by Claudius Salmasius?
questions.explanation: Claudius Salmasius wrote Defensio Regia pro Carolo I in 1649 to which Milton replied in 1651.

questions.question: In 'Defensio Secunda' (1654), Milton fiercely attacked Alexander More, though the anonymous Royalist tract 'Regii Sanguinis Clamor' was actually authored by:
questions.explanation: Peter du Moulin the Younger wrote Regii Sanguinis Clamor though Alexander More oversaw its printing.

questions.question: The title page of Milton's 1649 tract 'The Tenure of Kings and Magistrates' explicitly declares that it is lawful to depose and put to death:
questions.explanation: The subtitle states that it is lawful for any who have the power to call to account a tyrant or wicked king.

questions.question: In 'Eikonoklastes', what specific charge did John Milton level against King Charles I regarding a prayer included in 'Eikon Basilike'?
options: It was copied verbatim from Thomas More's 'Utopia'
It was translated directly from Machiavelli's 'Discourses'
It was stolen from a Catholic liturgy of the Virgin Mary
It was plagiarized from Pamela in Philip Sidney's 'Arcadia'
questions.explanation: Milton exposed that the king prayer was adapted from the pagan heroine Pamela in Sidney Arcadia.

questions.question: Milton's Sonnet 16, composed in May 1652 to address Oliver Cromwell, opens with which exact apostrophe?
options: Avenge, O Lord, thy slaughtered saints
Fairfax, whose name in arms through Europe rings
Vane, young in years, but in sage counsel old
questions.explanation: Sonnet 16 opens with the line Cromwell, our chief of men, who through a cloud / Not of war only.

questions.question: To which prominent Commonwealth statesman did John Milton address the 1652 sonnet praising him as 'young in years, but in sage counsel old'?
questions.explanation: Milton addressed Sonnet 17 to Sir Henry Vane the Younger praising his statesmanship and wisdom.

questions.question: In his poignant 1658 sonnet 'Methought I saw my late espoused saint', which mythical figure does Milton cite who was rescued from the grave?
questions.explanation: Milton compares his deceased wife Katherine Woodcock to Alcestis brought back from death by Hercules.

questions.question: In February 1653, to which President of the Council of State did John Milton dispatch a letter warmly recommending Andrew Marvell?
questions.explanation: Milton wrote to Lord President John Bradshaw commending Marvell knowledge of Latin and French.

questions.question: What is the exact metrical and stanzaic form of Andrew Marvell's 'An Horatian Ode upon Cromwell's Return from Ireland'?
options: Heroic couplets in decasyllabic rhyming pairs
Four-line stanzas of two iambic tetrameter and two iambic trimeter lines
Spenserian nine-line stanzas in iambic pentameter
questions.explanation: Marvell Horatian Ode uses an aabb stanza consisting of two four-foot lines and two three-foot lines.

questions.question: In 'An Horatian Ode', how does Andrew Marvell famously characterize King Charles I on the Whitehall scaffold?
options: As a royal actor upon a tragic scaffold
As a crowned martyr upon a sacrificial altar
As an unyielding tyrant defying public law
As an exiled monarch seeking foreign aid
questions.explanation: Marvell dignified portrayal states That thence the royal actor borne / The tragic scaffold might adorn.

questions.question: At Nun Appleton House between 1650 and 1652, whom was Andrew Marvell employed to tutor in languages and geography?
questions.explanation: Marvell tutored twelve-year-old Mary Fairfax the only daughter of retired General Thomas Fairfax.

questions.question: Which commemorative poem did Andrew Marvell publish anonymously in 1655 to praise the first full year of Cromwell's Protectorate?
options: Upon the Hill and Grove at Bill-borow
The First Anniversary of the Government Under His Highness the Lord Protector
A Poem upon the Death of His Late Highness
questions.explanation: Marvell published The First Anniversary in 1655 celebrating Cromwell rule and national recovery.

questions.question: To which Royalist friend and brother of the deceased poet Sidney Godolphin did Thomas Hobbes dedicate 'Leviathan' in 1651?
questions.explanation: Hobbes dedicated Leviathan to Francis Godolphin of Godolphin in honor of his brother Sidney.

questions.question: In Part 2 of 'Leviathan', what collective metaphor does Thomas Hobbes apply to the artificial person of the sovereign state?
options: The absolute shepherd of the faithful
The grand magistrate of natural law
That mortal god under the immortal God
questions.explanation: Hobbes terms the Commonwealth that great Leviathan or that mortal god to which we owe peace.

questions.question: What is the specific title of the fourth and final part of Thomas Hobbes's 'Leviathan', which attacks church abuses and scholasticism?
options: Of the Dominion Paternal and Despotical
questions.explanation: Part 4 of Leviathan is entitled Of the Kingdom of Darkness criticizing religious superstitions.

questions.question: Which French artist and printmaker designed the famous 1651 engraved title page for Thomas Hobbes's 'Leviathan'?
questions.explanation: The iconic title page depicting the crowned figure composed of citizens was engraved by Abraham Bosse.

questions.question: To which English political leader was James Harrington's 1656 republican masterpiece 'The Commonwealth of Oceana' dedicated?
questions.explanation: Harrington dedicated Oceana to His Highness the Lord Protector of the Commonwealth of England.

questions.question: In the allegorical framework of 'The Commonwealth of Oceana', under which persona is Oliver Cromwell represented as model lawgiver?
questions.explanation: Harrington models the heroic founder and Lord Archon Olphaus Megaletor directly upon Oliver Cromwell.

questions.question: In 1659, at which London venue did James Harrington and his circle meet nightly to debate political rotation and the secret ballot?
options: Will's Coffee House in Bow Street
The Devil Tavern at Temple Bar
The Mermaid Tavern in Bread Street
Miles's Coffee House in New Palace Yard
questions.explanation: Harrington founded the Rota Club in 1659 meeting at Miles Coffee House at the sign of the Turk Head.

questions.question: Which London bookseller, operating from St Dunstan's Churchyard in Fleet Street, published the first edition of 'The Compleat Angler' in 1653?
questions.explanation: Richard Marriot in St Dunstan Churchyard Fleet Street published Walton The Compleat Angler in 1653.

questions.question: In Chapter 4 of 'The Compleat Angler', a milkmaid and her mother sing paired pastoral lyrics composed by which two Elizabethan poets?
options: Edmund Spenser and Sir Philip Sidney
Christopher Marlowe and Sir Walter Ralegh
questions.explanation: They sing Marlowe The Passionate Shepherd to His Love and Ralegh reply The Nymph Reply to the Shepherd.

questions.question: In the expanded 1676 edition of 'The Compleat Angler', which younger poet and friend of Walton authored Part II on fly-fishing?
questions.explanation: Charles Cotton wrote Part II Being Instructions how to angle for a Trout or Grayling in a clear Stream.

questions.question: To which Norfolk gentleman and friend did Sir Thomas Browne address the epistle dedicatory of 'Hydriotaphia, Urne-Buriall' in 1658?
questions.explanation: Browne dedicated Hydriotaphia to his worthy and honored friend Thomas Le Gros of Crostwick.

questions.question: The unearthing of roughly forty ancient funeral urns in which Norfolk field directly prompted Sir Thomas Browne's 'Hydriotaphia'?
questions.explanation: Browne records that about forty or fifty urns were found in a field at Old Walsingham in Norfolk.

questions.question: In the concluding chapter of 'Hydriotaphia', Sir Thomas Browne delivers which memorable aphorism concerning human mortality?
options: Oblivion is an impossible haven for mortal fame
Man is a noble animal, splendid in ashes, and pompous in the grave
All things began in order and shall end in darkness
Nature is the art of God
questions.explanation: Browne writes this famous observation in chapter 5 reflecting on monument vanity.

questions.question: To which Norfolk worthy did Sir Thomas Browne dedicate his botanical and mystical treatise 'The Garden of Cyrus' in 1658?
questions.explanation: Browne dedicated The Garden of Cyrus to Nicholas Bacon of Gillingham.

questions.question: Under the patronage of the Earl of Carbery, at which Carmarthenshire estate did Jeremy Taylor reside while writing 'Holy Living'?
questions.explanation: Jeremy Taylor was protected during the Interregnum at Golden Grove seat of the Earl of Carbery.

questions.question: Which landmark theological treatise advocating liberty of conscience had Jeremy Taylor published in 1647 prior to 'Holy Living'?
questions.explanation: Taylor published The Liberty of Prophesying in 1647 defending freedom of religious conscience.

questions.question: Rather than standard dramatic acts, into what five structural units did Sir William Davenant divide 'The Siege of Rhodes' in 1656?
questions.explanation: Davenant styled the five sections of The Siege of Rhodes as Entries borrowing a masque convention.

questions.question: Which English architect and disciple of Inigo Jones designed the innovative perspective stage sets for 'The Siege of Rhodes'?
questions.explanation: John Webb designed the changeable painted wings and shutters for the stage at Rutland House in 1656.

questions.question: What historical military event provides the dramatic milieu for Davenant's 1656 production of 'The Siege of Rhodes'?
options: The 1453 siege of Constantinople by Mehmed II
The 1571 battle of Lepanto by Selim II
The 1522 siege of Rhodes by Solyman the Magnificent
The 1683 siege of Vienna by Kara Mustafa
questions.explanation: The opera depicts the heroic defense of Rhodes by the Knights Hospitaller against Sultan Solyman.

questions.question: Where was Sir William Davenant imprisoned under sentence of death by Parliament while he continued writing 'Gondibert'?
questions.explanation: Davenant was captured at sea and held in the Tower of London, where he continued writing Gondibert.

questions.question: What striking emblem adorns the engraved title page of Henry Vaughan's 1650 collection 'Silex Scintillans'?
options: A flint heart struck by divine lightning and weeping tears
A pelican feeding its young with blood
A flaming heart ascending towards an altar
A caged bird looking out at an olive branch
questions.explanation: The Latin title Silex Scintillans means the flashing flint and depicts a stony heart struck by God.

questions.question: Which poem in 'Silex Scintillans', opening 'Happy those early days! when I / Shined in my angel-infancy', influenced Wordsworth's Ode?
questions.explanation: The Retreat reflects upon childhood innocence and directly inspired Wordsworth Immortality Ode.

questions.question: Which Latin-titled poetic collection by Henry Vaughan, celebrating his native River Usk, was published in 1651 without his supervision?
questions.explanation: Olor Iscanus meaning The Swan of Usk was published in London in 1651 by Vaughan friend Thomas Powell.

questions.question: In the authorial preface to his 1656 'Poems', what dramatic resolution did Abraham Cowley announce regarding his public life?
options: That he had converted to the Presbyterian covenant
That he had abandoned public strife to seek quiet retirement
That he intended to write the definitive history of the regicide
That he would wage relentless poetic war against Cromwell
questions.explanation: Cowley declared his desire to retire peacefully and bury all past civil hostilities.

questions.question: What defining formal structure characterized the irregular odes pioneered by Abraham Cowley in his 1656 collection?
options: Rigid heroic couplets with identical caesura placement
Quantitative dactylic hexameters following Latin rules
Strict triadic structure of strophe, antistrophe, and epode
Unfixed line lengths and irregular stanzaic rhyme patterns
questions.explanation: Cowley Pindarique Odes discarded classical triads in favor of flexible meters and rhyme schemes.

questions.question: When King Charles II noted in 1660 that Waller's Restoration poem was inferior to his ode on Cromwell, how did Edmund Waller reply?
options: The muse of sorrow sings louder than the muse of joy
A subject's verses must yield to a sovereign's majesty
Poets, Sir, succeed better in fiction than in truth
Kings command kingdoms, but imagination commands poets
questions.explanation: Waller witty reply to Charles II has become one of the most famous rejoinders in literary history.

questions.question: Which celebrated apostrophe to the River Thames appears in the 1655 authorized text of Sir John Denham's 'Cooper's Hill'?
options: Roll on, thou deep and dark blue Ocean, roll
Sweet Thames, run softly, till I end my song
Thy forest, Windsor! and thy green retreats
O could I flow like thee, and make thy stream / My great exemplar, as it is my theme
questions.explanation: These four lines in the revised text of Cooper Hill set a standard for neoclassical balanced verse.

questions.question: Within Katherine Philips's Society of Friendship in Wales, what pastoral pseudonym was assigned to her closest friend Anne Owen?
questions.explanation: Katherine Philips addressed numerous poems of passionate friendship to Lucasia Mrs Anne Owen.

questions.question: Despite Katherine Philips's ardent royalism, what prominent public role was held by her husband James Philips during the Commonwealth?
options: A Cavalier general in the Royalist army
A Parliamentarian commissioner and Member of Parliament
An Anglican bishop ejected from his diocese
questions.explanation: James Philips was an active Parliamentarian and High Court commissioner in Wales.

questions.question: Which natural philosophy treatise did Margaret Cavendish publish in 1655 to challenge both Cartesian dualism and Hobbesian materialism?
options: The Description of a New World
questions.explanation: Margaret Cavendish published Philosophical and Physical Opinions in 1655 detailing her vitalist theory.

questions.question: To which supreme ruler did Gerrard Winstanley dedicate his 1652 utopian agrarian treatise 'The Law of Freedom in a Platform'?
questions.explanation: Winstanley addressed The Law of Freedom directly to His Excellency Oliver Cromwell urging agrarian reform.

questions.question: In the 1649 manifesto 'The True Levellers Standard Advanced', Gerrard Winstanley proclaimed that the earth was originally made to be:
options: A common treasury for all mankind
A feudal estate for noble landlords
A private inheritance for righteous saints
questions.explanation: Winstanley declared that the earth was made a common treasury for all humans without landlords.

questions.question: In October 1649, which outspoken Leveller leader was tried for high treason at the Guildhall in London and triumphantly acquitted?
questions.explanation: John Lilburne known as Freeborn John conducted his own defense and won a total acquittal.

questions.question: Which radical Ranter preacher authored the sensational 1649 pamphlet 'A Fiery Flying Roll', which Parliament ordered to be burned?
questions.explanation: Abiezer Coppe published A Fiery Flying Roll in 1649 warning the rich of divine apocalyptic wrath.

questions.question: Which massive ecclesiastical work in eleven books did the church historian Thomas Fuller publish in London in 1655?
options: The Holy State and the Profane State
questions.explanation: Fuller published The Church-History of Britain from the birth of Jesus Christ until the year 1648 in 1655.

questions.question: What was the title of the famous collection of Commonwealth drolls and farcical stage sketches published by Francis Kirkman in 1672?
options: A Short View of the Immorality of the Stage
The Wits, or Sport upon Sport
questions.explanation: Francis Kirkman published The Wits or Sport upon Sport in 1672 collecting drolls staged during the ban.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Commonwealth Period (1649–1660) is NOT correct?
options: Sir William Davenant staged 'The Siege of Rhodes' in 1656
John Milton served as Latin Secretary to the Council of State
Thomas Hobbes published 'Leviathan' in London in 1651
Public theatres operated freely throughout London with state subsidies
questions.explanation: Public theatres were strictly closed by parliamentary order during the entire Commonwealth era.

questions.question: Which of the following literary milestones regarding the Interregnum is NOT correct?
options: John Milton completed and published the twelve-book 'Paradise Lost' in 1652
Izaak Walton issued the first edition of 'The Compleat Angler' in 1653
Andrew Marvell wrote 'Upon Appleton House' while tutoring Mary Fairfax
Sir Thomas Browne published 'Hydriotaphia' and 'The Garden of Cyrus' in 1658
questions.explanation: Milton did not publish Paradise Lost in 1652; it appeared in ten books in 1667 and twelve books in 1674.
